Both cite the two jobs and the failure class. In reading.rs, the six direct check calls in check_reading_acceptance are replaced by a call to refusing_check, which runs the same six checks in the same order through step!. No check body changed. The fix sits in the shared gate, the corpus and mechanism tests, and the planner rule.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md gains a rule: a plan that adds or changes a refusal or matching rule must list the input forms it handles, run the rule against the stored corpus, and cite the results in the plan; the planner prompt stays within its 1300-token budget.
criteria.evidence: planner.md gains 'Refusal or matching rule: map each input form to a refusal_corpus case.' REFUSAL_CORPUS_RULE in the planner brief's Report section adds the full rule: list the input forms, map each to a corpus case by id or to a case a plan step adds, and make `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` a demonstration. summary: The change passes. It names the root cause in CHANGELOG.md, in decisions entry D148, and in the doc comments on `refusing_check` and the corpus file: refusal and matching rules were never run against real request and reading shapes before they were planned or landed. It fixes this in the shared place where readings are accepted or refused, not in one job's check. `refusing_check` now runs the same six checks as before, one `step!` line each and in the same order, and reports which check refused. `check_reading_acceptance` is now a thin wrapper around it, and no check body changed. A new test file, crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs, holds 18 labeled request shapes, each with the outcome it must get. A mechanism test fails if any check in the gate has no corpus case where it refuses. The planner prompt gets a short clause and the planner brief gets the full rule, and a briefs test checks both. I ran the corpus tests (6 passed), the new briefs test, the planner budget test and the CLI budget tests, and all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed, and the replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused. Two things fall short, neither blocking. The planner rule says to map input forms to corpus cases and leave the run to the producer and verifier, instead of the criterion's "run and cite results"; this is reasonable because the planner can only read files. The mechanism cannot see changes to the request parser, stem lists or stop lists; the change states this limit and narrows it by pinning bullet counts.
